name: AI Pumpkin Head Photoshoot: The Halloween Trend From One Photo
blurb: The pumpkin head photoshoot is the October photo where your head is a carved jack-o'-lantern, usually in a field or a pumpkin patch; people also call the pictures pumpkin head photos.

prompts.text: Use the uploaded image as the base. Keep the person's body, body shape, skin tone, hands and outfit exactly the same as in the photo: the same clothes, colors, fabrics, shoes and accessories. Replace only the head with a large, real carved pumpkin worn over the head, as in a real pumpkin head photoshoot: a big, round, ribbed orange jack-o'-lantern, clearly bigger than a human head, with a short curved green stem on top. Its bottom sits right on the shoulders and the collar, with a soft natural shadow where it meets the clothes, so it clearly looks worn and not floating, and no neck shows. The carved face has two triangle eyes, a triangle nose and a wide grin with a few square teeth. A warm candle glow shines from inside through the carved holes, and inside the holes there is only that glow, never skin or a face. If the person has long hair, a little of it falls from under the pumpkin onto the shoulders. The person sits on an old wooden chair in the middle of a wide, open field of tall, dry, golden grass, legs crossed, hands resting on the knee, body facing the camera. It is dusk: a deep blue sky with a last band of orange light on the horizon, a few bare trees far away and a thin mist low over the grass. Soft, dim light still shows the outfit clearly. Full body from the top of the pumpkin to the shoes, with the chair and the grass in frame. Camera at chest height, 35mm lens, shot on film: soft natural film grain, muted warm and teal colors, gentle contrast. Photorealistic, a real photo, not CGI, not a cartoon. Moody and a little spooky, but fun. Vertical 9:16. Exactly one person, five fingers on each hand. No human face, no text, no logos.
